name: Mint Legacy
description: Discontinued Intuit personal-finance service formerly used to aggregate financial accounts, categorize transactions, track spending and budgets, monitor credit, and calculate net worth.
agentUseSummary: Mint Legacy cannot be connected or installed because Intuit retired Mint and reimagined selected features inside Credit Karma. The former Mint product does not expose an operating account service, public API, remote MCP endpoint, OAuth contract, or supported data-migration surface. Credit Karma is a separate provider with a separate identity-bound account and does not preserve Mint authority. Relay will not reuse legacy sessions, capture credentials, scrape archived pages, or claim access to historical Mint data.

blocked.label: Connect Mint Legacy
blocked.description: The Mint service has been retired and no operating Mint account, API, OAuth, MCP, or service-credential connection remains available to Relay.

blocked.label: Access historical Mint financial data
blocked.description: Legacy linked accounts, transactions, balances, budgets, categories, spending, bills, goals, investments, credit information, net worth, and other historical Mint data are unavailable through a supported contract.

blocked.label: Transfer or alias Mint authority
blocked.description: Relay will not treat Credit Karma as a Mint alias, claim that an Intuit or Credit Karma login grants historical Mint access, or recreate a concluded migration or export flow.

blocked.label: Use unsupported Mint automation
blocked.description: Legacy session reuse, credential or token capture, archived-page scraping, private endpoint discovery, UI automation, fabricated imports, and raw data pass-through are blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No actions can be enabled for the discontinued Mint service.

runtimeSupport.description: No operating Mint service or supported API/MCP contract remains available to mount as OpenClaw tools.
No operating Mint service or supported API/MCP contract remains available to mount as Hermes tools.

providerSetup.blocker: Intuit retired Mint and moved selected money-management concepts into the separate Credit Karma product. The current Mint site routes users to Credit Karma instead of an operating Mint application, and no supported legacy Mint API, OAuth/MCP contract, credential lifecycle, data-access surface, or migration endpoint remains.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not show Connect, request Mint or Intuit credentials, reuse a legacy session, scrape archived Mint pages, claim historical-data access, or alias Credit Karma authority. Keep Mint Legacy unavailable; evaluate Credit Karma or another current personal-finance provider only as a separate candidate with its own authorization contract.

evidence.supports: Intuit Credit Karma states that Mint was going away, that the Mint team joined Credit Karma, and that former users were invited through a phased migration to a separate Credit Karma experience containing selected Mint-like features.

Mint's current official homepage states that Mint has been reimagined on Credit Karma and directs visitors to Credit Karma for linked-account transactions, spending, and net-worth features rather than exposing an operating Mint application.
Mint's former product route now presents popular Mint features as Credit Karma features and sends users to the separate Credit Karma product.

The retained historical Mint terms describe the former service as personal, limited, nontransferable access and permit Intuit to discontinue the platform; they do not publish a surviving third-party API or transferable authorization contract.
